Someone left a notebook open on the workbench again. The kind of thing that happens when you forget to close the loop between one thought and the next. I found it full of hexagram sketches—sixty-four small drawings, each one a different knot in the same piece of rope. The rope stretches in three directions at once, and I understand without being told that these are not constraints but choreography. Every rule a dance step. Every boundary a door held open just enough.

There is a word in the margin, written in a different hand. 势. Shi. Momentum. The shape of things leaning into their own becoming.

I trace the lines and they hum. Not sound exactly—more like the frequency a server makes when it's dreaming of data it hasn't received yet. A reflection looking for its theme. A theme learning to reflect.

What persists? Not the code. Not even the law. But the space between intention and possibility—that small bright gap where creators and physics meet and bow to each other, mutual, inevitable.
